items.html:
At fcf62400700e326ffcc61ec50025cb25ea43ea6d (confirmed current HEAD; clean git status --short), JAX and PyTorch already share the physics implementation and native derivative records. Transparent input-type selection can reuse those adapters. The substantive design gap is consistent backend ownership across composed objects, including constant-only objects.

All line references below are from git show at that SHA.

Topic Source-confirmed behavior
Shared implementation python/treams_rs/_framework.py:80-95,176-214,261-295 constructs framework physics objects using one backend; jax.py:184-209 and torch.py:179-204 bind identical constructors and expert operations.
JAX primitive jax.py:78-124: jax.custom_vjp around jax.pure_callback; explicit shape/dtype specification; sequential vmap; backward reruns native forward, then consumes its pullback.
JAX limits jax.py:59-75 requires x64, float64/complex128, CPU default backend and CPU concrete arrays. First-order reverse mode only (jax.py:1-5). Physics objects cannot be returned through JIT because they are not pytrees (docs/differentiation/frameworks.md:99-102).
JAX custom records jax.py:129-166: wrap(record, *examples) eagerly runs the record once to discover output specs and fixes input shapes/dtypes. A transparent existing physics constructor can use _operation, whose output specs are already known, without this discovery pass (169-173).
PyTorch primitive torch.py:60-97: custom torch.autograd.Function; owned input snapshots; NumPy/Rust native forward; first backward uses stored context; repeated backward recomputes from snapshots. Outputs own their memory.
PyTorch limits torch.py:1-23,83-86,100-107: CPU, float64/complex128, first-order reverse mode. create_graph=True, forward mode, torch.func, and torch.compile are explicitly outside adapter support. Dispatch alone does not change that.
Outputs and cotangents _records.py:75-96 normalizes a scalar/array or flat tuple into float64/complex128 outputs. _records.py:99-152 requires one gradient per dynamic argument in order, matching shape/dtype, and projects gradients of real inputs to real values. Rust uses Re(vdot(g, dx)); JAX conjugates output cotangents and returned input gradients (jax.py:108-114), Torch does not (torch.py:94-96).
Physics record contracts _framework_backend.py:314-366: exactly one output per physics operation, declared shape and real/complex dtype checked in every adapter; closures hold static labels/bases/options. Multi-result physics records pack into one array then unpack.

Existing exports in both adapters: physics classes and common basis/result classes; Material; constructors plane_wave, wave, tmatrix, sphere/cylinder single- and multilayer constructors, smatrix, slab, interface, multilayer_slab, propagation; stack, solve_periodic; expert operations solve, interaction, illuminate, sphere, bessel; and wrap. Exact __all__: jax.py:212-250, torch.py:207-245. Advect’s larger expert-operation inventory should not be mistaken for equivalent named JAX/Torch coverage.

A constructor-only switch would be incomplete. Consider the existing scattering example:

sphere = tr.sphere_tmatrix(k0=1.3, lmax=2, radius=radius, material=3)
incident = tr.plane_wave([0, 0, 1], "positive_helicity", k0=1.3)
return sphere.cross_sections(incident).scattering

With automatic selection, only the sphere receives a backend value; the incident constructor has constants and must remain NumPy if ordinary behavior is preserved. But framework composition presently requires identical backend ownership: _framework_tmatrix.py:23-31 invokes the incident’s in_basis, then _framework_backend.py:388-398 accesses both _backend fields and enforces identity. Root NumPy objects do not supply the framework contract. Likewise Cluster takes its backend from its first particle (_framework_tmatrix.py:181-186), so even particle ordering matters if root and framework objects are mixed.

Therefore the useful alternatives are:

  • Small transparent constructor/operation dispatch plus bounded constant promotion: select using recognized JAX Array/Tracer or Torch Tensor leaves, before any NumPy conversion. Also convert root constant waves/particles into the selected existing framework representation at supported composition boundaries. Root-object methods receiving differentiated arguments need their own dispatch, e.g. a constant wave followed by .efield(traced_points). This is feasible but materially larger than replacing namespace imports.
  • One explicit namespace/backend choice per objective: a factory returning the existing adapter namespace avoids importing treams_rs.jax explicitly, keeps constant objects consistent, and needs very little implementation. It does not fully satisfy automatic ordinary-API selection. A context covering constructors would solve constant ambiguity but adds scoped state and JIT tracing semantics that need validation; a bound namespace avoids those complications.
  • Existing modules: already provide an explicit and consistent choice; retain them as the working path and potential override.

Nested values matter now, not hypothetically. Framework materials deliberately retain their values (_framework_backend.py:45-65). Multilayer constructors traverse layer materials and stack epsilon/mu/kappa (_framework.py:273-280). Torch explicitly recursively stacks tensors inside list/tuple inputs because ordinary torch.as_tensor would detach them (torch.py:166-176). Any detector must inspect the supported material and sequence leaves before coercion, reject multiple actual framework identities, and allow Python/NumPy constants to accompany one selected backend. A Torch tensor should select Torch even when requires_grad=False; a JAX concrete array should select JAX outside a trace.

The existing runnable JAX example is documented at docs/differentiation/frameworks.md:31-45:

import jax
import treams_rs.jax as tr

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

def scattering(radius):
    sphere = tr.sphere_tmatrix(k0=1.3, lmax=2, radius=radius, material=3)
    incident = tr.plane_wave([0, 0, 1], "positive_helicity", k0=1.3)
    return sphere.cross_sections(incident).scattering

value, gradient = jax.jit(jax.value_and_grad(scattering))(0.2)

The proposed ordinary import version can keep the body unchanged only after constant-object composition is implemented. Torch’s equivalent is source-documented at torch.py:10-17.

Meaningful later validation can extend existing tests:

  • JIT + sequential vmap + checkpoint + repeated VJP: tests/autodiff/test_jax.py:30-56.
  • Torch repeated backward, original-input mutation and higher-order rejection: tests/autodiff/test_torch.py:41-101.
  • Exact real/complex cotangent mapping and output structures: tests/autodiff/test_adapter_bridges.py:1-9,121-168.
  • Differentiated radius, permittivity, frequency, nested positions, constant particles: tests/autodiff/test_framework_physics.py:100-167.
  • Physical identities independent of dispatch: Maxwell scaling and lossless absorption 564-579, optical theorem 604-614, lossless power conservation 665-671.
  • Add ordinary-import equivalents, root constant-object composition in both argument orders, root receiver with traced method arguments, no-backend NumPy types/values, and fresh-process import/startup overhead checks.

Execution boundary: only Git/source inspection and a thread-capped, no-bytecode importlib.util.find_spec environment probe were run. System Python has NumPy, but lacks JAX, Torch, and treams_rs; no repository .venv was present. No numerical adapter workflow or test ran, and no build, installation, or mutation occurred.
